script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The narrator says the king asks once more; the king does not say those words.
The earlier request needs a reference to Esther 5:6–8.
Esther asks for her people’s lives, not specifically for her family. The explanation conflates the two.
Being queen does not establish that Esther is not short on palaces.
Esther does not ask for a job or title here, but the text does not say she wants neither.
The text says Esther identifies Haman, not that she points at him.
Esther 2:21–23 does not say the king later remembers the report. In Esther 6:1–3, the record is read to him.
The text says Haman stood in terror, not that he was frozen in his seat. It also does not specify that this was a minute after he was a guest at the table.
The text does not say the king needed to step away or that he went to cool off. A reason for his action cannot be added, even as a guess.
The text says the king was furious, but it does not say he was not sad.
Haman’s face is covered immediately, but the text does not establish that he never had a chance to explain himself.
The text does not say that covering Haman’s face meant a verdict was already in.
The fact that Mordecai was Esther’s cousin needs a reference to Esther 2:7.
The text does not say Haman picked out timber for the gallows.
The text does not establish that Hegai had nothing to do with the gallows.
Hathach’s return message to Esther is in Esther 4:9, outside the cited verses.
The text does not say whether the king hesitated or considered a second opinion.
